questions.q: Using the Euclidean algorithm, what is the highest common factor of 252 and 198?
questions.e: Apply repeated division: 252 = 198 + 54; 198 = 3×54 + 36; 54 = 36 + 18; 36 = 2×18. The last non-zero remainder is 18, so HCF = 18.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Mathematics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.topic: Mensuration / comparison of cylinder and cone volumes
questions.q: A cylinder and a cone have the same circular base radius and the same height. What is the ratio of their volumes (cylinder : cone)?
questions.e: The cylinder’s volume is πr²h, while the cone’s volume is (1/3)πr²h. With the same radius and height, the cylinder holds three times the volume of the cone. Therefore the ratio is 3 : 1.
tags: Mensuration / comparison of cylinder and cone volumes

questions.q: What are the roots of 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0?
questions.e: Factorise 2x² − 5x + 3 as (2x − 3)(x − 1) = 0. Therefore x = 3/2 or x = 1. Substitution confirms both values satisfy the original equation.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Mathematics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A box measures 3 cm by 4 cm by 12 cm. What is the straight-line distance between two opposite vertices?
questions.e: The space diagonal of a cuboid is √(l²+b²+h²). Substituting gives √(3²+4²+12²) = √(9+16+144) = √169 = 13 cm. This applies the three-dimensional Pythagorean theorem.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Mathematics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: What is the distance between the points (2, −1) and (8, 7) on a Cartesian plane?
questions.e: Use √[(x₂−x₁)²+(y₂−y₁)²]. The horizontal and vertical differences are 6 and 8, so distance = √(36+64) = √100 = 10 units. This is the Pythagorean theorem applied to the coordinate differences.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Mathematics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular decagon?
questions.e: A decagon has 10 sides. The sum of its interior angles is (10−2)×180° = 1,440°. In a regular decagon all angles are equal, so each angle is 1,440°÷10 = 144°.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Mathematics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “The officer was asked to be ______ while discussing the taxpayer’s confidential information.”
questions.e: Discreet is an adjective meaning careful, tactful or prudent in speech and conduct. Discrete means separate or distinct. The sentence needs the adjective describing the officer’s conduct: discreet.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Cambridge Dictionary — English Usage.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “The new index will ______ the existing records by adding missing cross-references.”
questions.e: Complement means to complete, improve or go well with something. Compliment means an expression of praise. Because the index adds something useful to the existing records, complement is correct.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Cambridge Dictionary — English Usage.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Choose the correct pronoun: “The officer to ______ the complaint was addressed forwarded it for examination.”
questions.e: The preposition “to” requires an object. Whom is the objective form of who, so “to whom the complaint was addressed” is grammatically correct.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: British Council LearnEnglish — Relative Pronouns.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A warning says that a cyclone is likely to strike within the next few hours. Which adjective best describes the danger?
questions.e: Imminent means about to happen or likely to occur very soon. Eminent means distinguished or famous, while immanent has a different philosophical meaning. An approaching storm is imminent.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Cambridge Dictionary — English Usage.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “The investigator used follow-up questions to ______ further details from the witness.”
questions.e: Elicit is a verb meaning to draw out or obtain information, a response or a reaction. Illicit is an adjective meaning illegal or not permitted. Follow-up questions are intended to elicit details.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Cambridge Dictionary — English Usage.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “The inspection vehicle remained ______ while the documents were checked.”
questions.e: Stationary means not moving. Stationery refers to writing materials such as paper, envelopes and pens. Since the sentence describes a vehicle that did not move, stationary is correct.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Cambridge Dictionary — English Usage.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Which word completes the phrase “the ______ reason for rejecting the application” when the intended meaning is “the main reason”?
questions.e: Principal can function as an adjective meaning main or most important. Principle is a noun meaning a rule, standard or fundamental belief. The sentence needs the adjective “principal reason”.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Cambridge Dictionary — English Usage.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Under the Khasi Hills Autonomous District Council’s Administration of Elaka (Amendment) Act 2023, what is a Dorbar Shnong?
o: A traditional village institution composed of adult inhabitants
A court consisting only of district judges
questions.e: The KHADC Act defines a Dorbar Shnong as a traditional institution of a village or shnong, composed of adult inhabitants according to customary practices. It is convened as required and presided over by the Rangbah Shnong or recognised village headman.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Meghalaya Gazette — KHADC Administration of Elaka Amendment Act 2023.

questions.q: Which two channels are formed when the Kynshi River bifurcates to create Nongkhnum River Island?
questions.e: Meghalaya Tourism explains that Nongkhnum River Island is formed where the Kynshi splits into the Phanliang and Namliang rivers. The bifurcation encloses the island in West Khasi Hills.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Meghalaya Tourism — Nongkhnum River Island.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: How does Meghalaya Tourism describe Kyllang Rock in the Khasi Hills?
o: A natural monolith shaped like a giant grey dome
questions.e: Kyllang Rock is described by Meghalaya Tourism as an impressive natural monolith, a giant grey dome rising from pine forests in the Khasi Hills. It is a geological landform, not a cave or lake.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Meghalaya Tourism — Kyllang Rock.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Siju Cave in South Garo Hills is primarily known as which type of cave?
questions.e: Meghalaya Tourism identifies Siju as a limestone cave, also known as Dobakkol or the Bat Cave. Its stalactites, stalagmites and underground passages are characteristic limestone cave features.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Meghalaya Tourism — Siju Cave.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Under Article 165 of the Constitution, who appoints the Advocate-General for a State?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: Article 165 provides that the Governor of each State appoints a person qualified to be appointed as a High Court judge to be Advocate-General for the State. The Advocate-General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: After a State Legislative Assembly passes the special resolution required by Article 169, which body may create or abolish that State’s Legislative Council by law?
questions.e: Article 169 empowers Parliament to provide by law for the creation or abolition of a State Legislative Council, but only after the State Assembly passes the prescribed special-majority resolution. The resolution itself does not create or abolish the Council.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India

questions.q: The constitutional document that presents a State Government’s estimated receipts and expenditure for a financial year is called the ______.
questions.e: Article 202 calls the State’s annual statement of estimated receipts and expenditure the Annual Financial Statement. It is the constitutional basis of the State Budget and is laid before the Legislature for each financial year.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India

questions.q: Under Article 203, a demand for a grant in a State Legislative Assembly cannot be made except on whose recommendation?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: Article 203(3) provides that no demand for a grant shall be made except on the recommendation of the Governor. The Legislative Assembly then votes on the demands, subject to the constitutional rules.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India

questions.q: Which subject is expressly protected from discussion in a State Legislature by Article 211?
o: The conduct of a Supreme Court or High Court judge in discharge of judicial duties
A report of the State Public Service Commission
A motion of no confidence in the Council of Ministers
questions.e: Article 211 bars discussion in a State Legislature with respect to the conduct of a Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court in the discharge of duties. It protects judicial independence from legislative debate on individual judicial conduct.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India

questions.q: Which of the following is a constitutional duty of a Chief Minister under Article 167?
o: To communicate decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor and furnish information when required
To audit the accounts of the State Government
questions.e: Article 167 requires the Chief Minister to communicate to the Governor the decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and legislative proposals, furnish information requested by the Governor, and submit specified matters for Council consideration.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Government of India, Legislative Department — Constitution of India.

questions.q: Which Greek envoy is traditionally associated with the work Indica, an account of India during the Mauryan period?
questions.e: Megasthenes served as an envoy of Seleucus I to the court of Chandragupta Maurya. His work Indica is an important literary source for reconstructing aspects of Mauryan society and administration, although it survives mainly through later quotations.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT History Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Who composed the Allahabad Pillar inscription (Prayaga Prashasti) praising Samudragupta?
questions.e: The Prayaga Prashasti on the Allahabad Pillar was composed by Harisena, a court poet and official of Samudragupta. The inscription records the ruler’s achievements and is a major source for Gupta political history.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT History Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: The book Kitab-ul-Hind, which discusses Indian society, religion and knowledge, was written by whom?
questions.e: Al-Biruni, the Central Asian scholar, wrote Kitab-ul-Hind after studying Indian texts and traditions. His work is valued for its analytical descriptions of Indian learning, customs and religious ideas.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT History Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: In the Delhi Sultanate, what did an iqta primarily represent?
o: A hereditary private ownership grant of all land
An assignment of revenue from a territory to an official in return for service
questions.e: An iqta was principally a revenue assignment given to an officer or military commander. It did not ordinarily make the holder the private owner of the land; the holder collected assigned revenue under the Sultanate’s administrative system.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT History Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: In the Mughal mansabdari system, what did the rank zat indicate?
o: The personal rank and status of the mansabdar
The land revenue of a province
The number of villages under direct ownership
questions.e: Zat indicated the mansabdar’s personal rank and position in the imperial hierarchy. Sawar related to the cavalry obligation or number of horsemen to be maintained. The two figures served different administrative purposes.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT History Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Which Khasi leader is associated with Hima Khatsaw Phra and the resistance against British expansion in the early nineteenth century?
questions.e: Meghalaya Tourism identifies Hima Khatsaw Phra as the ancestral home of U Tirot Singh, who led a rebellion against British forces. His resistance began in 1829 and remains an important part of Khasi history.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: Meghalaya Tourism — Hima Khatsaw Phra.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: What was the central electoral arrangement agreed under the Poona Pact of 1932 for the Depressed Classes?
o: Nomination of all representatives by the Governor-General
questions.e: The Poona Pact replaced the separate-electorate arrangement proposed for the Depressed Classes with reserved seats in joint electorates. It was concluded between B. R. Ambedkar and representatives of the caste-Hindu leadership in September 1932.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT History Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: An oxbow lake is most commonly formed when which river feature is cut off from the main channel?
questions.e: A river meander may become increasingly curved until the river cuts through the narrow neck during high flow. Deposition seals the old loop from the main channel, leaving an oxbow lake.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Geography Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A radial drainage pattern is most likely to develop where streams flow outward from which type of landform?
o: A central dome or volcanic cone
A flat basin with no central highland
questions.e: In a radial pattern, streams diverge outward from a central elevated feature such as a dome, volcanic cone or isolated hill. The direction of flow radiates away from the high point.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Geography Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A dendritic drainage pattern generally develops where the underlying rock has which characteristic?
o: Strongly alternating bands of hard and soft rock
Relatively uniform resistance with little structural control
A circular basin surrounded by hills
questions.e: Dendritic drainage resembles the branching pattern of a tree. It commonly develops on relatively uniform rock or unconstrained terrain where streams are not strongly guided by joints, faults or alternating resistant strata.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Geography Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Why do tropical cyclones rarely originate very close to the Equator?
o: Sea surface temperatures are always too low
The Coriolis force is too weak to provide sufficient initial rotation
Air pressure is always higher than elsewhere
There is no moisture in equatorial air
questions.e: The Coriolis force is zero at the Equator and increases with latitude. A tropical cyclone needs sufficient initial rotation to organise its circulation, so it rarely forms within a few degrees of the Equator.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Geography Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Spring tides occur when the Sun, Earth and Moon are approximately aligned at which lunar phases?
questions.e: At new moon and full moon, the gravitational effects of the Sun and Moon act along nearly the same line. Their combined effect produces a larger tidal range, called a spring tide.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Geography Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Why are surface waters in many subtropical ocean belts relatively saline?
o: Evaporation commonly exceeds precipitation and freshwater input is limited
Sea ice melts throughout the year
questions.e: In many subtropical high-pressure belts, dry descending air suppresses rainfall while evaporation remains substantial. With limited freshwater input, surface salinity tends to be relatively high.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Geography Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: How is Net Domestic Product (NDP) calculated from Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?
questions.e: Depreciation, also called consumption of fixed capital, measures the loss in value of fixed assets through use and obsolescence. Subtracting it from GDP gives NDP: NDP = GDP − depreciation.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Economics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: The net barter terms of trade are commonly measured as which ratio multiplied by 100?
o: Import price index divided by export price index
Export price index divided by import price index
Export volume divided by import volume
Foreign exchange reserves divided by imports
questions.e: Net barter terms of trade compare export prices with import prices: (Export Price Index ÷ Import Price Index) × 100. An improvement means a given quantity of exports can purchase relatively more imports.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Economics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Which pair of characteristics defines a pure public good?
questions.e: A pure public good is non-rival, so one person’s use does not reduce the amount available to others, and non-excludable, so people cannot readily be prevented from benefiting. National defence is a standard example.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Economics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: If the Government fixes a binding price ceiling below the market equilibrium price, what is the likely immediate market result, other things being equal?
o: A surplus because supply exceeds demand
A shortage because demand exceeds supply
An automatic increase in equilibrium price
questions.e: A binding ceiling prevents the price from rising to equilibrium. At the lower controlled price, consumers want to buy more while producers are willing to supply less, creating excess demand or a shortage.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Economics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: On the conventional 0-to-1 scale, what does a Gini coefficient of 0 represent?
o: Equal government expenditure in every district
questions.e: A Gini coefficient of 0 represents perfect equality, while a value of 1 represents maximal inequality on the conventional scale. Some publications multiply the coefficient by 100, but the interpretation remains the same.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Economics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: If the Indian rupee depreciates against the US dollar, what is the usual direct effect on the rupee cost of an unchanged dollar-priced import?
o: It is unaffected by the exchange rate
questions.e: Depreciation means more rupees are required to buy one US dollar. Therefore, an import priced in dollars costs more in rupees, assuming the foreign-currency price and other costs remain unchanged.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Economics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: In a human nephron, where does blood filtration first produce the filtrate that enters Bowman’s capsule?
questions.e: The glomerulus is a tuft of capillaries enclosed by Bowman’s capsule. Blood pressure drives water and small dissolved substances through the filtration barrier into the capsular space, while blood cells and most large proteins remain in the blood.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Science and Biology Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Which structural feature makes the alveoli of human lungs efficient sites for gas exchange?
o: Thick dry walls with little blood supply
Very thin moist walls and a dense capillary network
A large muscular layer that pumps oxygen
questions.e: Alveoli provide a large surface area. Their thin, moist walls and close contact with capillaries create a short diffusion distance, allowing oxygen to enter blood and carbon dioxide to leave it efficiently.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Science and Biology Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Atoms of the same element are called isotopes when they have the same number of ______ but different numbers of ______.
questions.e: An element is defined by its proton number (atomic number). Isotopes share that number but have different neutron counts, so their mass numbers differ. Their chemical behaviour is broadly similar because their electronic structure is similar.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Science and Biology Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: What is the main way a catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction?
o: It permanently increases the amount of reactants
It provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy
It changes the equilibrium constant in every reaction
It is consumed completely as a reactant
questions.e: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy. It increases the rate at which equilibrium is reached but is not consumed overall and does not change the equilibrium constant at a fixed temperature.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Science and Biology Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Specific heat capacity is the heat energy required to raise the temperature of what amount of a substance by one kelvin?
o: One cubic metre by one degree Celsius
questions.e: Specific heat capacity is energy required to raise the temperature of unit mass by one kelvin. In SI units it is expressed in joules per kilogram per kelvin (J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹).
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Science and Biology Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A persistent pollutant is found at a higher concentration in the tissues of top predators than in organisms lower in the food chain. What is this process called?
questions.e: Biomagnification is the increase in concentration of a persistent substance at successive trophic levels. Organisms at higher levels consume many contaminated organisms and may accumulate greater concentrations of substances such as DDT or methylmercury.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Science and Biology Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Which group of ecosystems is most directly associated with coastal blue carbon storage?
o: Mangroves, salt marshes and seagrass beds
Coral reefs, glaciers and conifer forests
questions.e: NOAA describes coastal blue carbon as carbon captured and stored by coastal ecosystems, especially mangroves, salt marshes and seagrass beds. Much of this carbon is stored for long periods in waterlogged coastal soils and sediments.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NOAA National Ocean Service — Blue Carbon.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: NOAA National Ocean Service — Blue Carbon

questions.q: In UNESCO’s biosphere-reserve zonation, which zone is intended for strict long-term protection of ecosystems and biodiversity?
questions.e: The core area is the legally protected zone devoted to long-term conservation of biodiversity. The buffer zone allows compatible activities around or next to it, while the transition area supports sustainable human and economic activity with local communities.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme — Biosphere Reserve Zonation.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme — Biosphere Reserve Zonation

questions.q: Which approach best describes bioremediation of contaminated soil or groundwater?
o: Using microorganisms to degrade or detoxify contaminants
Covering the site with concrete without treatment
Increasing the concentration of pollutants to precipitate them
Using only mechanical filtration to remove all soil
questions.e: Bioremediation uses microorganisms, commonly bacteria and sometimes fungi or other microbes, to degrade or detoxify contaminants. EPA guidance explains that conditions may be managed to encourage microbial activity in soil or groundwater.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: US EPA — Introduction to In Situ Bioremediation of Groundwater.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: US EPA — Introduction to In Situ Bioremediation of Groundwater

questions.q: Under the EIA public-consultation framework, which two components are generally recognised?
o: A public hearing and written responses from other concerned persons
A court trial and a parliamentary vote
A wildlife census and a forest settlement report
A social-media poll and a referendum
questions.e: The EIA public-consultation process includes a public hearing at or near the project site to ascertain local concerns and written responses from other concerned persons with a plausible stake. It is a consultation mechanism, not a court trial or referendum.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: MoEFCC — EIA Notification 2006 and Public Consultation guidance.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: MoEFCC — EIA Notification 2006 and Public Consultation guidance

questions.q: A rectangular grid has 3 rows and 2 columns of equal small rectangles. How many rectangles of all sizes can be formed using the grid lines?
questions.e: Choose any two of the four horizontal grid lines and any two of the three vertical grid lines. That gives C(4,2)×C(3,2) = 6×3 = 18 possible rectangles, including the six smallest cells.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Mathematics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: In classical propositional logic, what is the truth value of the implication P → Q when P is false and Q is true?
questions.e: A material implication P → Q is false only when P is true and Q is false. If the antecedent P is false, the implication is true regardless of Q; therefore it is true in the stated case.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: OpenStax Contemporary Mathematics — Key Concepts: Conditional Statements.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: OpenStax Contemporary Mathematics — Key Concepts: Conditional Statements

questions.q: Five clerks A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north. C is immediately to the right of A, E is at the far right, B is immediately to the left of E, and D sits to the left of A. Who occupies the middle seat?
questions.e: E must be fifth and B fourth. Since C is immediately right of A and D is to the left of A, the remaining positions force D–A–C–B–E. The middle, third seat is occupied by C.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Mathematics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: If M > N, N > P and P > Q, which statement must be true?
questions.e: The inequalities form a descending chain M > N > P > Q. By transitivity, M is greater than Q. The other statements reverse or contradict the given order.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Mathematics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A machine moves the alphabetically earliest remaining word to the leftmost unfilled position at each step. If the input is “mango, apple, guava, banana”, what is the arrangement after the second step?
questions.e: Step 1 moves apple to the first position. Among the remaining words, banana is alphabetically earliest, so step 2 places it second. The unfilled positions retain mango and guava in their original relative order.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Mathematics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: Statement: Several streetlights in a town have remained unlit for weeks despite complaints. Actions: I. Inspect the reported locations and repair defective lights. II. Switch off all streetlights in the town to reduce electricity use. Which action logically follows?
questions.e: The problem is failure of specific streetlights. Inspecting and repairing the affected units directly addresses the stated problem. Shutting down all streetlights would worsen public safety and is not a reasonable response to the complaints.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Mathematics Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: What is the primary role of a DHCP server on an IP network?
o: To encrypt every file stored on a computer
To automatically provide network configuration such as an IP address to a client
To convert domain names into IP addresses
To filter spam messages from email accounts
questions.e: DHCP follows a client-server model and provides host configuration parameters, including dynamically allocated network addresses. It reduces manual configuration and can reuse addresses when a client no longer needs them.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: IETF RFC 2131 — Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: IETF RFC 2131 — Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol

questions.q: How many bits are used in an IPv6 address?
questions.e: RFC 8200 specifies that IPv6 expands the IP address size from IPv4’s 32 bits to 128 bits. The larger address space supports far more addressable nodes and more flexible addressing hierarchy.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: IETF RFC 8200 — Internet Protocol Version 6.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: In the OSI reference model, which layer is principally associated with logical addressing and routing packets between networks?
questions.e: The Network layer is responsible for logical addressing and routing packets across interconnected networks. The Data Link layer handles local frame delivery on a link, while the Physical layer transmits raw bits.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: ITU-T Recommendation X.200 — OSI Basic Reference Model.
questions.label: Original Practice
questions.sourceName: ITU-T Recommendation X.200 — OSI Basic Reference Model

questions.q: Which security property is directly supported by a valid digital signature?
o: Confidentiality of the entire message by itself
Authenticity of the signer and detection of unauthorised data changes
questions.e: A digital signature can authenticate the signatory and help detect unauthorised modification of signed data; it can also support non-repudiation. It does not, by itself, encrypt the message or guarantee confidentiality.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NIST FIPS 186-5 — Digital Signature Standard.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: In a spreadsheet formula, what does the reference $B$4 indicate?
o: Both the column and row are fixed when the formula is copied
Only the row changes when copied
Only the column changes when copied
Both the row and column change automatically
questions.e: The dollar signs make both the column B and row 4 absolute. When a formula containing $B$4 is copied to another cell, that reference remains $B$4 instead of shifting relative to the new location.

questions.topic: CGST Act Section 18 / credit in special circumstances
questions.q: A person becomes liable for GST registration and applies within the statutory 30-day period. Under Section 18(1)(a) of the CGST Act, which stock-related credit may be available once registration is granted?
o: Only credit on capital goods purchased after registration
Credit on eligible inputs in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held immediately before the liability date
Credit on all personal purchases made during the previous year
Credit on every exempt supply made before registration
questions.e: Section 18(1)(a) allows eligible input tax credit on inputs in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held on the day immediately preceding the date the person becomes liable to pay tax, provided the statutory registration conditions and time limit are met.

questions.topic: CGST Act Section 132 / previous sanction for prosecution
questions.q: Which CGST Act provision requires the Commissioner’s previous sanction before a person may be prosecuted for an offence under Section 132?
questions.e: Section 132(6) states that no person shall be prosecuted for an offence under that section except with the previous sanction of the Commissioner. The sanction requirement is a statutory precondition to prosecution, not a summons power.

questions.topic: CGST Act Section 127 / residual penalty procedure
questions.q: Where the CGST Act makes a penalty imposable but does not provide a separate procedure for that penalty, what safeguard does Section 127 require before the penalty is imposed?
o: A reasonable opportunity of being heard
Approval by the GST Council in every individual case
A criminal conviction in every case
questions.e: Section 127 allows the proper officer to impose a penalty in cases not covered by a separate penalty procedure, but only after giving the person concerned a reasonable opportunity of being heard. The provision is a residual procedural safeguard.

questions.q: Under Section 128 of the CGST Act, which authority may waive specified penalties or late fees by notification on the recommendation of the GST Council?

questions.q: A business has total assets of ₹8,40,000 and total liabilities of ₹3,10,000. Using the accounting equation, what is the owner’s capital?
questions.e: The accounting equation is Assets = Liabilities + Capital. Rearranging gives Capital = Assets − Liabilities = ₹8,40,000 − ₹3,10,000 = ₹5,30,000. The equation must remain balanced after each recorded transaction.

questions.q: A trader receives ₹12,000 from a customer who previously owed that amount. Which journal entry correctly records the receipt?
questions.e: Cash increases, so the Cash Account is debited. The customer’s outstanding receivable decreases, so the Customer or Debtor Account is credited. The entry is Debit Cash ₹12,000 and Credit Customer ₹12,000.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Accountancy Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A trial balance shows equal debit and credit totals. Which conclusion is justified?
o: The books are guaranteed to be completely error-free
Some types of error may still exist despite equal totals
Every transaction has been recorded in the correct account
questions.e: Agreement of a trial balance is a useful arithmetic check, but it does not detect every error. Complete omission, errors of principle and compensating errors can leave debit and credit totals equal while the accounts remain incorrect.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Accountancy Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: What is the main purpose of preparing a Bank Reconciliation Statement?
o: To calculate depreciation on bank equipment
To explain differences between the bank balance in the cash book and the balance shown by the bank statement
To replace the cash book with the passbook
questions.e: A Bank Reconciliation Statement reconciles the bank-column balance in the cash book with the balance shown by the bank statement or passbook on a particular date. Timing differences and recording errors commonly explain the difference.
questions.source: Original Practice — not an official PYQ. Source: NCERT Accountancy Textbooks.
questions.label: Original Practice

questions.q: A machine costs ₹1,20,000, has an estimated residual value of ₹20,000 and a useful life of five years. Under the straight-line method, what is the annual depreciation charge?
questions.e: Straight-line depreciation = (Cost − Residual Value) ÷ Useful Life. Here (₹1,20,000 − ₹20,000) ÷ 5 = ₹1,00,000 ÷ 5 = ₹20,000 per year, assuming no change in estimates.

questions.topic: Financial accounting / capital and revenue expenditure
questions.q: A department purchases a new computer server expected to be used for several years. How should the purchase price normally be classified in the accounts?
questions.e: The purchase of a durable asset expected to provide benefits over more than one accounting period is normally capital expenditure. Routine maintenance and small repairs that merely keep an asset operating are generally revenue expenditure.
